mainTopic: Late קידוש and הבדלה, using beer for קידוש and הבדלה, how much wine to drink, and the meaning of 'סמוך למנחה'
overview: This amud opens with רבא's final ruling: someone who already ate can still make קידוש or הבדלה, a missed קידוש can be made all שבת day, and a missed הבדלה can be made later in the week. אמימר teaches a version that allows a late הבדלה only on Sunday. A story follows in which אמימר fasted rather than make הבדלה on beer, and a year later accepted beer as חמר מדינה, the main local drink. The גמרא learns three הלכות from his conduct. Next, רב חסדא, רב and שמואל rule that beer may not be used for קידוש or הבדלה, and several Sages express their dislike of beer. Two ברייתות then teach that the כוס של ברכה must be wine, and that the תנאים argue about קידוש on beer. The גמרא rules that one must drink a מלא לוגמא of the קידוש wine. Finally, it returns to the משנה and asks whether 'סמוך למנחה' means מנחה גדולה or מנחה קטנה, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's ruling on late קידוש and הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that tasting food does not cancel קידוש or הבדלה, that a missed Friday-night קידוש can be made all שבת day, and that a missed הבדלה can be made later in the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that someone who already tasted food can still make קידוש, and someone who already tasted food can still make הבדלה. Someone who did not make קידוש on Friday night can make it all day long, until שבת ends. Someone who did not make הבדלה on מוצאי שבת can make it during the whole week.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final halacha after the earlier debate: eating first does not cancel your obligation, and there is extra time to make up a missed קידוש or הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions held that once you eat, you can no longer make קידוש or הבדלה. רבא rules that the obligation stays even after eating. He also sets the make-up windows: for קידוש, the rest of שבת day; for הבדלה, 'the whole week'.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is (the final practical ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: In the last line, 'כל השבת כולו' does not mean 'all of שבת.' Here 'שבת' means the week. Most ראשונים explain it as the first three days of the week, which still count as 'after שבת.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that a missed הבדלה can be made up until Tuesday, and that a missed Friday-night קידוש can be made during שבת day.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is:
one who tasted food may still recite kiddush,
and one who tasted food may still recite havdala,
and one who did not recite kiddush on Shabbat eve
may go on reciting kiddush the entire day
until the conclusion of Shabbat.
One who did not recite havdala at the conclusion of Shabbat
may go on reciting havdala the entire week.
phrases.notes: 'שבת' here means the week, which ראשונים explain as the first three days

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final halacha for the earlier debate (on the previous amud) about eating before קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating first does not cancel קידוש or הבדלה. Missed קידוש can be made all שבת day. Missed הבדלה can be made during the week.

steps.title: אמימר's version of רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אמימר quotes רבא with one change: a missed הבדלה can only be made up during the next day (Sunday), not the whole week.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר taught this teaching of רבא in this wording: רבא said, the הלכה is that someone who tasted food can make קידוש, and someone who tasted food can make הבדלה. Someone who did not make קידוש on Friday night can make it all day long. Someone who did not make הבדלה on מוצאי שבת can make it all day long (only on Sunday).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's ruling, as taught by אמימר. The only real difference is the time limit for a missed הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a missed הבדלה can be made up 'כל השבת כולו', meaning during the week. In אמימר's version it is 'כל היום כולו', meaning only the following day, Sunday. Everything else is the same, so the dispute is only about how long the make-up window for הבדלה lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened with it / taught it

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful to compare the last line with step 1. It is almost identical, but 'כל היום כולו' (one day) replaces 'כל השבת כולו' (the week).

phrases.aramaic: אַמֵּימָר פָּתַח לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרָבָא
phrases.english: Ameimar began this teaching of Rava
in this formulation:
Rava said: The halacha is:
one who tasted may recite kiddush; one who tasted may recite havdala;
one who did not recite kiddush on Shabbat eve
may go on reciting kiddush the entire day;
one who did not recite havdala at the conclusion of Shabbat
may go on reciting havdala the entire day (of Sunday only).
phrases.notes: This is the key change from step 1

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר פָּתַח לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרָבָא בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same ruling and narrows the time window for הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed הבדלה may be made up only during the next day.

steps.title: אמימר refuses beer for הבדלה and fasts
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's sons tell רב אשי that אמימר visited them and they had no wine. He would not make הבדלה on beer, so he went to sleep without eating. The next day they brought wine, and he made הבדלה and then ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר ינוקא and מר קשישא, the sons of רב חסדא, told רב אשי: Once אמימר came to our town and we had no wine. We brought him beer, but he did not make הבדלה on it, and he went to bed fasting. The next day we worked hard and brought him wine, and he made הבדלה and then ate something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how אמימר actually behaved. This story will later serve as the source for several halachos.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר did not consider beer good enough for הבדלה, so he waited for wine. Because he had not yet made הבדלה, he did not eat at all that night. He made הבדלה the next day, which shows in practice that a late הבדלה is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: We worked hard / made an effort

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ מָר יָנוֹקָא וּמָר קַשִּׁישָׁא
phrases.english: Mar Yanuka and Mar Kashisha said to him,
sons of Rav Chisda, to Rav Ashi:
Once Ameimar happened to come to our place,
and we did not have wine.
We brought him beer,
and he did not recite havdala, and he spent the night fasting.
The next day, we exerted ourselves and brought him wine,
and he recited havdala and tasted something.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ מָר יָנוֹקָא וּמָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a real-life case involving אמימר that connects to the rules about late הבדלה.
steps.raayaObject: That הבדלה can be made the next day, and that one may not eat before הבדלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אמימר's own conduct as reported by רב חסדא's sons.

steps.title: Beer as the local wine
steps.stepSummary: A year later the same thing happened, and this time אמימר made הבדלה on beer, ruling that where wine is hard to get, beer counts as חמר מדינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year he came to our town again. We had no wine, so we brought beer. He said: If so, if wine is this hard to get here, this beer is the wine of the land. He made הבדלה on it and ate something.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. אמימר changes his practice and creates the concept of חמר מדינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first time, אמימר assumed the lack of wine was temporary. Now he sees that wine is regularly unavailable in this town, so beer serves as the local 'wine' and is valid for הבדלה. The status of a drink depends on what is normal and important in that place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Wine of the land': the main local drink, which can be used in place of wine

steps.whyThisMatters: חמר מדינה is the halachic source for making הבדלה on drinks other than wine, such as beer, when they are the main beverage of the place.

phrases.english: The next year he again came to our place,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה לַן חַמְרָא, אַיְיתִינָא שִׁיכְרָא,
phrases.english: we did not have wine, so we brought beer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אִי הָכִי, חֲמַר מְדִינָה הוּא,
phrases.english: He said: If so, it is the wine of the province.
He recited havdala and tasted something.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אִי הָכִי, חֲמַר מְדִינָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story, and אמימר issues a new ruling based on the changed situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where wine is not normally available, the main local drink (חמר מדינה) may be used for הבדלה.

steps.title: Three lessons learned from אמימר's conduct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws three הלכות from the story: הבדלה in תפילה still requires הבדלה on a cup, eating before הבדלה is forbidden, and a missed הבדלה can be made up later in the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. First: someone who said הבדלה in תפילה still has to make הבדלה over a cup. Second: a person is forbidden to eat before making הבדלה. Third: someone who did not make הבדלה on מוצאי שבת can make it during the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the story by listing three הלכות that come out of what אמימר did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר surely said אתה חוננתנו in his שמונה עשרה, yet he still waited to make הבדלה on a cup, which is lesson 1. He fasted all night rather than eat, which is lesson 2. He made הבדלה the next day, which proves that late הבדלה works, lesson 3. The גמרא phrases lesson 3 in the wording of the first version of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a case)
One who said הבדלה in תפילה (אתה חוננתנו)

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכות: (1) Tasting food does not cancel קידוש or הבדלה. (2) Missed קידוש can be made all שבת day. (3) Missed הבדלה can be made later, either the whole week (the first three days) or only Sunday, depending on the version. (4) הבדלה in תפילה does not exempt הבדלה on a cup. (5) Do not eat before הבדלה. (6) חמר מדינה may be used in place of wine.
steps.confusionAlert: Since אמימר made הבדלה only one day late, his story fits both versions of רבא. Yet the גמרא states lesson 3 as 'כל השבת כולו' (the week). Do not assume the story by itself settles the dispute between the two versions.

phrases.english: Learn from this three things.
Learn from it: one who recites havdala in prayer
must recite havdala over a cup.
And learn from it: it is prohibited for a person
to eat before he recites havdala.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הִבְדִּיל בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: And learn from it: one who did not recite havdala at the conclusion of Shabbat
may go on reciting havdala the entire week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws halachic conclusions from the story told in steps 3 and 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הבדלה in davening does not exempt הבדלה on a cup. Eating before הבדלה is forbidden. A missed הבדלה can be made up later in the week.

steps.title: רב הונא asks whether one may make קידוש on beer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks רב חסדא whether קידוש may be made over שיכרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא asked רב חסדא: What is the law about making קידוש on beer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about beer. It is linked to the story of אמימר, who refused to make הבדלה on beer. רב הונא asks a real question: can beer be used for קידוש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is the normal drink for קידוש. The question is whether another drink, beer, can take wine's place. This sets up the whole discussion of whether beer counts for these ceremonies.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna asked Rav Chisda:
What is the law about making Kiddush over beer?
phrases.notes: אַשִּׁיכְרָא is just עַל שִׁיכְרָא squeezed into one word.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a fuller discussion of the beer issue raised by אמימר's story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שיכרא is acceptable for קידוש.

steps.title: רב חסדא answers: better drinks were never approved, so certainly not beer
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the question about better drinks was never resolved, going all the way back to רבי, so beer is certainly not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Barley beer, fig beer, and berry beer are better drinks. I asked רב about them, רב asked רבי חייא, and רבי חייא asked רבי. Nobody ever settled that question. Do you even need to ask about date beer?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers with a 'how much more so' argument. If better drinks were never approved for קידוש, plain beer is certainly not approved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about better drinks passed through three generations of teachers without an answer. So no one had a source allowing them. Since date beer is lower in quality, it is obviously not allowed for קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if even… (opens a 'how much more so' argument)

steps.confusionAlert: 'He did not resolve it' does not mean the better drinks were allowed. It means no one had a source permitting them. That uncertainty is exactly why beer is clearly not allowed.

phrases.english: He said: Now, if
barley beer, fig beer, and berry beer,
phrases.notes: These are considered better drinks than date beer.

phrases.english: which I asked Rav about,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא, וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא מֵרַבִּי,
phrases.english: and Rav asked Rabbi Chiya, and Rabbi Chiya asked Rebbi,
and he did not resolve it for him,
is date beer even a question?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Beer may not be used for קידוש, by a קל וחומר from better drinks that were never approved.

steps.title: Listeners infer that beer is barred for קידוש but allowed for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: People who heard רב חסדא concluded that his answer applied only to קידוש, so הבדלה on beer would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: it is only קידוש that we do not make over beer, but הבדלה we do make over it.
steps.whatsHappening: Listeners draw a conclusion from רב חסדא's answer. This step sets up the next move, where רב חסדא will correct them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא spoke only about קידוש, so people read his silence about הבדלה as permission. Their reasoning was that קידוש may be more demanding than הבדלה. This conclusion is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (often a mistaken conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase סבור מינה usually signals a conclusion the גמרא is about to reject. Do not take it as the halacha.

phrases.english: They understood from it
that it is Kiddush that we do not make over it,
but Havdalah we do make over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a narrow conclusion from רב חסדא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed inference: beer is barred only for קידוש, not for הבדלה.

steps.title: רב חסדא corrects them: no הבדלה on beer either
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes רב: beer cannot be used for קידוש, and in the same way it cannot be used for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: This is what רב said: Just as we do not make קידוש over beer, we also do not make הבדלה over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects the listeners' conclusion. Beer is excluded from both קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listeners thought הבדלה might be easier than קידוש. רב treats the two the same: a drink not good enough for one is not good enough for the other. This explains why אמימר at first refused to make הבדלה on beer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for אמימר's first refusal. His later ruling, that beer counts when it is חמר מדינה (the standard local drink), is an exception for places where wine is truly hard to get.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא: הָכִי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to them: This is what Rav said:
Just as we do not make Kiddush over it,
so too we do not make Havdalah over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא: הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that הבדלה on beer is allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The listeners assumed הבדלה is easier than קידוש. רב rules that both follow the same rule.

steps.title: שמואל says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that שמואל also ruled that beer is barred for both קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב תחליפא בר אבימי said in the name of שמואל: Just as we do not make קידוש over beer, we also do not make הבדלה over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from another great teacher. שמואל agrees with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רב and שמואל, the two leading teachers of that generation, say the same thing in the same words, the ruling is strongly established.
steps.whatToRemember: Beer is treated the same for קידוש and הבדלה: neither may be made on it, according to both רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi said that Shmuel said:
Just as we do not make Kiddush over it,
so too we do not make Havdalah over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling with the same ruling from שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that beer is barred for both קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל, as reported by רב תחליפא בר אבימי.

steps.title: רבי praises an excellent beer sent by Levi
steps.stepSummary: לוי sent רבי a very strong beer. רבי tasted it and said it was good enough for קידוש and for all the songs of praise in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי sent רבי a beer made with thirteen soakings. He tasted it, and it was very pleasant. He said: A drink like this is fit for קידוש, and for saying over it all the songs and praises in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about an especially fine beer. The story connects to the topic of whether beer can be used for קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This beer was made by soaking thirteen batches of dates in the same water, which made it very rich in taste. רבי's praise suggests that a high-quality beer could be worthy even of קידוש. That stands in contrast to the plain beer discussed above.

keyTerms.meaning: Soakings (batches of dates soaked in the water)

phrases.english: Levi sent to Rebbi
a beer of thirteen soakings.
He tasted it, and it was very pleasant.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כְּגוֹן זֶה רָאוּי לְקַדֵּשׁ עָלָיו
phrases.english: He said: Something like this is fit to make Kiddush over

phrases.aramaic: וְלוֹמַר עָלָיו כׇּל שִׁירוֹת וְתוּשְׁבָּחוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: and to say over it all the songs and praises in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ruling to a story about an unusually good beer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי praised a very high-quality beer as fit for קידוש.

steps.title: The beer hurt רבי at night
steps.stepSummary: That night the beer gave רבי stomach pain. He said that beer hurts and then soothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: At night it caused him pain. He said: It pains, and then it soothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a twist. The beer that tasted wonderful made רבי sick that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's comment gives a balanced view: beer brings both pleasure and pain. This leads into the next statements, where other teachers speak strongly against drinking beer.

phrases.english: At night, it caused him pain.
He said: It pains, and it soothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story of רבי and the beer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beer brings both pleasure and pain.

steps.title: רב יוסף vows never to drink beer
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he would make a public vow never to drink beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I will take a vow in public that I will not drink beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the theme of beer's bad effects. רב יוסף shows how strongly he wanted to stay away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow made in public is very hard to cancel. By choosing that kind of vow, רב יוסף shows a firm and lasting decision. This was notable because beer was a common drink in בבל.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: I will vow in public
that I will not drink beer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a teacher's personal stance against beer after the story of the pain it caused.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף firmly refused to drink beer.

steps.title: רבא would rather drink flax water than beer
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he would rather drink the water used to soak flax than drink beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I would drink flax-soaking water, and I would not drink beer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an even stronger statement against beer. He would prefer a disgusting drink over beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water used to soak flax was foul and unpleasant. By choosing it over beer, רבא shows how much he disliked beer, likely because of the harm it does to the body.
steps.whatToRemember: Halacha: beer is not used for קידוש or הבדלה (רב and שמואל), except when it is the standard local drink (חמר מדינה), as אמימר ruled in step 4. The statements of רבי, רב יוסף and רבא show that the teachers also had personal reservations about drinking beer.

phrases.english: Rava said: I would drink flax-soaking water
and I would not drink beer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger personal statement against beer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא prefers even foul water to beer.

steps.title: רבא: Whoever makes קידוש on beer should end up drinking beer
steps.stepSummary: רבא sharply criticizes making קידוש over beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Whoever makes קידוש over beer, may his regular drink be beer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another sharp line against beer. Someone who makes קידוש on it deserves to be poor and drink only beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל, beer was the drink of poor people. רבא is saying that treating beer as important enough for קידוש is disrespectful to the מצוה. The fitting result is that the person will become poor and have nothing else to drink.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
May his drink be beer
phrases.notes: A curse-like expression: he should become poor.

phrases.english: whoever makes Kiddush over beer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's negative attitude toward beer from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making קידוש on beer is improper. The person deserves to be reduced to drinking only beer.

steps.title: רב הונא finds רב making קידוש on beer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא sees רב making קידוש on beer and explains it with a light remark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא found רב making קידוש over beer. He said: 'אבא has started earning coins from beer.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story. רב הונא sees his teacher רב making קידוש on beer and comments that רב has started earning money from beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אבא' was רב's personal name. רב had begun selling beer, so beer had become an important drink to him, and that is why he used it for קידוש. This is surprising, because in step 9 רב חסדא quoted רב himself as ruling that we do not make קידוש or הבדלה on beer. רב הונא's remark explains רב's conduct as the result of his personal situation, not as a general permission to use beer for קידוש.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אבא' here is not 'father'. It is רב's own name (אבא אריכא).

phrases.english: Rav — Rav Huna found him
making Kiddush over beer.
He said to him:
Abba has started to acquire
coins from beer.
phrases.notes: רב had become a beer seller, so beer was now precious to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story in which רב is seen making קידוש on beer, despite his own ruling in step 9. רב הונא explains it by beer's new importance to רב as a beer seller.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב made קידוש on beer, which רב הונא explained by beer's new importance to him.

steps.title: ברייתא: קידוש and ברכות only on wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that קידוש and ברכות are said only over wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: We make קידוש only over wine, and we make ברכות only over wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that limits קידוש and 'blessings' to wine. The next step will question the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half is clear: קידוש needs wine. The second half, 'ברכות only on wine', sounds too broad. It seems to say no ברכה may be said on any other drink, and that sets up the coming question.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We make Kiddush only over wine,
and we make blessings only over wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a formal source about what drink may be used, after the stories about beer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידוש and 'blessings' are said only over wine.

steps.title: But we do bless שהכל on beer and water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: we obviously say שהכל on beer and water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that over beer and water we do not say the ברכה of שהכל נהיה בדברו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second half of the ברייתא. Everyone knows you say שהכל before drinking beer or water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'ברכות only on wine' would mean that drinking beer or water gets no ברכה at all. That cannot be true. So the ברייתא must mean something narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה 'by Whose word all came to be'

phrases.english: Is that to say that over beer and water
we do not bless over them
'by Whose word all things came to be'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ואין מברכין אלא על היין'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain reading would forbid the obvious ברכה of שהכל on beer and water, which is clearly wrong.

steps.title: אביי: It means the כוס של ברכה for ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא only means that the כוס של ברכה for ברכת המזון must be wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what it means. We say 'Bring the cup of blessing to bless' only over wine.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. 'ברכות' in the ברייתא refers to the special cup used for ברכת המזון, not to every ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was never talking about the ordinary ברכה before drinking. It means that the formal 'cup of blessing' held during ברכת המזון must be wine. This keeps the ברייתא true and removes the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of blessing (used for ברכת המזון)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Only on wine' in the ברייתא means the כוס של ברכה for ברכת המזון, not the simple ברכה before drinking.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים ״הָבֵא כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה לְבָרֵךְ״
phrases.english: We do not say 'Bring a cup of blessing to bless'
except over wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid any ברכה on drinks other than wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the כוס של ברכה for ברכת המזון must be wine.

steps.title: ברייתא: Dispute about קידוש on beer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says no קידוש on beer, while רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: We do not make קידוש over beer. In the name of רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון they said: We do make קידוש over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with a מחלוקת. The first opinion forbids קידוש on beer, and רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the debate about beer as a formal תנאים argument. רבא's statements against קידוש on beer and the story of רב making קידוש on beer reflect these two sides.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not make Kiddush over beer.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon they said:
We do make Kiddush.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין עַל הַשֵּׁכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא directly about the beer question that the earlier stories discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: no קידוש on beer. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון: קידוש on beer is allowed.

steps.title: How much wine must be tasted for קידוש
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says any amount of wine is enough. רבי יוסי בר יהודה requires a מלא לוגמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One tastes any amount of wine. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: a cheekful.
steps.whatsHappening: The topic changes to how much wine the person making קידוש must drink. One view says even a tiny taste is enough, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה says a cheekful is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'מלא לוגמא' is enough liquid to fill one cheek. The question is whether just tasting the wine counts, or whether a real, noticeable drink is needed.

phrases.english: One tastes any amount of wine.
Rabbi Yosei son of Yehuda says:
A cheekful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which drink to use to how much of it to drink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: any amount versus a מלא לוגמא.

steps.title: רב and רב גידל: A cheekful is required
steps.stepSummary: רב, and also רב גידל from נרש, rule that you must taste a מלא לוגמא to be יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב, and רב גידל from נרש also taught: One who makes קידוש and tastes a cheekful is יוצא. If not, he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אמוראים who rule like רבי יוסי בר יהודה. Without a cheekful, you have not fulfilled קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not just a matter of doing it the best way. Less than a מלא לוגמא means the מצוה was not done. Two separate sources say the same thing, which makes the ruling stronger.
steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה: you must drink a מלא לוגמא for קידוש to count.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַב גִּידֵּל דְּמִן נָרֶשׁ:
phrases.english: and so taught Rav Giddel from Neresh:
One who makes Kiddush and tastes a cheekful — has fulfilled his obligation,
and if not — he has not fulfilled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַב גִּידֵּל דְּמִן נָרֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules like רבי יוסי בר יהודה from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלא לוגמא is required. Less means one is not יוצא.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: The name is just 'גידול'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he learned the teaching under the plain name גידול, with no other identification.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I learned it not as 'גידול בר מנשיא' and not as 'גידול בר מניומי', but just plain 'גידול'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק clarifies exactly whose name was on this teaching. In his version, it was simply 'גידול', with no father's name or other label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were several Sages named גידול. רב נחמן בר יצחק is careful to say his version did not tell us which one it was. The next step asks why this matters.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
I learned it
not as Giddul bar Menashya
and not as Giddul bar Minyumei
but as plain Giddul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the name of the teacher cited in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The teaching is credited simply to 'גידול', with no further identification.

steps.title: Why does the exact name matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it makes which גידול said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we care about the exact name. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha is the same no matter who said it. So the גמרא wants to know if this detail has any real use.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of step 23's name clarification.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it matters to identify exactly which גידול taught this.

steps.title: To compare his rulings against each other
steps.stepSummary: Knowing the exact Sage matters so we can tell whether his teachings contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: To raise a contradiction between his own statements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name matters for comparing a Sage's statements. If we know who said something, we can check it against his other rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two rulings come from the same Sage and seem to clash, we can raise a contradiction. If we do not know which גידול said this one, we cannot claim he contradicted himself.

keyTerms.meaning: His own statement against his own statement

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how carefully the גמרא tracks who said what. That care is what makes it possible to compare and question a Sage's statements.

phrases.english: To raise a contradiction between his own statement and his own statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exact identity matters for comparing, and possibly contradicting, one Sage's statements with his other statements.

steps.title: Which afternoon time does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'סמוך למנחה' and asks whether they mean close to מנחה גדולה or close to מנחה קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'close to מנחה.' The Sages asked: did we learn 'close to מנחה גדולה,' or perhaps we learned 'close to מנחה קטנה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of קידוש and goes back to the first words of our משנה. It asks which of the two afternoon times the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two famous afternoon times. מנחה גדולה is half an hour after midday, and מנחה קטנה is two and a half hours before sunset. The משנה just says 'close to מנחה' without saying which one, so the גמרא needs to pin down when eating becomes forbidden on ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to the time of מנחה (the משנה's phrase)
A question was asked among them (an open question the Sages were unsure about)
The 'great מנחה' time: half an hour after midday
The 'small מנחה' time: two and a half hours before sunset
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מנחה' means a TIME of day, not the prayer itself and not the flour offering. The two times are named after the stretch of the afternoon when the afternoon תמיד could be brought.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides how early in the day a person must stop eating on ערב פסח, so that he comes to the מצה with an appetite.

phrases.english: "Close to minḥa."
phrases.notes: Quoting the words of our משנה

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Did we learn 'close to the great minḥa'?
or perhaps
we learned 'close to the small minḥa'?
phrases.notes: Two and a half hours before sunset

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the קידוש and wine discussion (steps 21-25) and returns to the opening words of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'סמוך למנחה' in the משנה refers to מנחה גדולה or to מנחה קטנה.

steps.title: Reason for the first side: worry about the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first possibility: if the משנה means מנחה גדולה, the reason is the קרבן פסח, since a person who starts a meal might get carried away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we learned 'close to מנחה גדולה,' the reason is because of the קרבן פסח: perhaps he will get drawn into his meal (and fail to bring his offering in time).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now spelling out the reasoning behind each side of its question, starting with מנחה גדולה. It is setting things up; the reasoning for the other side (מנחה קטנה) comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח the קרבן פסח is slaughtered in the afternoon. If a person sits down to a big meal right after midday, he might stretch it out and neglect his offering. So on this side, the ban on eating starts early, at מנחה גדולה, to protect the קרבן פסח, not only to keep his appetite for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the קרבן פסח (the Pesach offering)
He will come to be drawn out (get carried away and keep eating)

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not the גמרא's answer. It is only the explanation of one side of the question. The sentence continues on the next amud with the other side.

phrases.english: Did we learn 'close to the great minḥa'
phrases.notes: Restating the first side in order to explain it

phrases.english: and that is because of the Pesach offering,
lest he come to be drawn out (in his meal),
phrases.notes: He might linger over a long meal and neglect slaughtering his קרבן פסח

steps.triggerLanguage: סָמוּךְ לְמִנְחָה גְּדוֹלָה תְּנַן וּמִשּׁוּם פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the first side (מנחה גדולה) of the question raised in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Continues the question by giving the reason for the מנחה גדולה side: concern that a long meal will make him neglect the קרבן פסח. The other side's reasoning follows.
